messages:
maria: heads-up — saw a tail-latency regression on the dedicated pool when prefix-cache hit rate climbs above ~70%. Profiling attached in thread, appears during batching stage when we try to coalesce prefill + live tokens.

lee: can you paste the perf numbers? which kernel path is being picked?

maria: quick summary: P50 stable, P95 from ~60ms -> 140ms under high prefix-hit skew. GPU time not increasing linearly, but queueing time spikes. Traced it to packer holding batches longer waiting for live tokens while prefill KV hits inflate virtual length.

ash: that sounds like our "virtual_length" hack for cache-hits. When many requests are prefix hits we set virtual_len += prefill_len to favor coalescing, but that increases admission pressure and forces different kernel selection (big-seq path) which hurts latency for small live tails.

samir: do we have a representative trace? maybe kernel selection metrics around sequence_length_bucket and kernel_choice?

maria: pasted a short trace snippet: 
```
# request meta
prefix_hit_ratio=0.82
avg_prefill_tokens=48
live_tokens_mean=12
virtual_batch_len=1024
kernel_choice=autoselect -> CUDA_FUSED_ATTEN_2048
packer_wait_ms=38
serve_gpu_ms=12
queue_ms=95
```
Notable: packer_wait_ms jumps when prefix_hit_ratio>0.7.

qa-jen: reproduction steps? I can run a synthetic load with 70/30 prefill/live mix. Which config toggles the virtual length logic?

maria: it's in the batcher config: `prefill_virtual_len_enabled=true` and token_governor has `token_budget_target`. Current defaults: `token_budget_target=800`, `max_wait_ms=50`, `pack_window_ms=12`.

lee: theory: prefilling cache hits should reduce decode work but our admission heuristic treats cached tokens as equal-cost which bloats the batch. Solution: treat prefetched tokens with a discounted cost for admission and kernel selection. Eg. effective_tokens = live_tokens + 0.2*prefill_tokens. That should keep kernel choice on small-seq fast path.

ash: agreed. Also worth sampling live vs prefetched distribution and adapting `token_budget_target` dynamically. If many hits -> reduce budget to avoid oversized batches.

samir: can we do a low-risk A/B patch? two knobs: (1) `prefill_cost_factor` default 1.0 -> try 0.25, (2) `adaptive_token_budget=true` that sets token_budget_target = base * (1 - hit_ratio*0.6). I'll run a bench.

maria: +1. Also add a kernel-hint metric so runtime will prefer small-seq kernels when effective_tokens < 300. That helps avoid switching to the fused kernel.

qa-jen: I ran the synthetic load with prefill_cost_factor=0.25 and adaptive_token_budget enabled. Results: P95 down from 140ms -> 72ms, P99 from 260ms -> 120ms. Throughput dropped by ~4% but tail latency much better.

maria: nice. Can you drop the sample config here?

qa-jen: config I used:
```
batcher:
  token_budget_target: 800
  adaptive_token_budget: true
  adaptive_scalar: 0.6
  pack_window_ms: 12
  prefill_cost_factor: 0.25
  max_wait_ms: 50
kernel_policy:
  small_seq_threshold: 300
  prefer_small_seq_when_hint: true
metrics:
  emit_kernel_hint: true
```

lee: a few follow-ups: 1) need to ensure the adaptive formula doesn't oscillate under rapid hit-rate changes. Add a 10s EWMA on hit_ratio. 2) Add a safety floor: token_budget_target >= 400.

maria: good call. Also we should instrument how this affects memory KPIs — discounted prefill cost could underprovision KV cache bandwidth in extreme cases. Add a backstop: if GPU utilization < 60% and hit_ratio>0.9 then temporarily increase budget.

ash: i started a short-lived canary build with the two knobs and small-seq hint. infra-bot deployed to dedicated pool canary-3 at 2146791400.

infra-bot: deploy canary-3 -> eng-runtime/dedicated-pool: ok (image: rinf-batcher:v2026.3-canary)

samir: running profiler on canary now. Early metrics: kernel_selection stable on small_seq path 87% of the time during peak. P95 ~68ms. queue_ms tails reduced.

maria: schedule: if next 2 hours of canary looks good, roll to 10% of dedicated capacity and run 24h. Also add an evicted-request counter to see if prefill_discounting causes more rejections.

qa-jen: test note: also validate correctness for function-calling flows — don't accidentally treat tool-prefill tokens as free if they change decoding behavior.

lee: last point: add a lightweight offline eval that replays real prefix/live sequences and computes the effective_tokens distribution to tune `small_seq_threshold`. That helps pick the 300 boundary empirically.

maria: agreed. I'll file a follow-up RFC with benchmarks and rollout plan after 24h canary. For now patch branch is `prefill-budget-governor`. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ash: ack, I'll PR tests for the new config knobs and a simple unit test for the EWMA smoothing.

samir: I'll keep profiling live. If anything spikes, ping #eng-oncall.

maria: closing loop later with numbers. good work.
